Both accessor rows carry `availableObjectFormats: [pe]` per [[D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY]] — declaring them on elf/macho would plant undefined imports, since glibc and libSystem have no such names — and the MACROS are pe-gated `variants` for the same reason, so on elf/macho they are 0-match and un-injected, leaving `_fmode`/`_environ` as ordinary identifiers there. ★ ACCEPTED COST, stated as the setlocale clause above states its own: `_environ` is a Microsoft spelling, so this descriptor's <stdlib.h> surface declares names the POSIX <stdlib.h> does not — but so does the REAL ucrt/stdlib.h, which is the header this descriptor shadows on pe, so on the format where these rows are visible the surface is MORE faithful, not less. WITNESS: examples/c/shipped_fmode_environ_pe RUNS both macros on pe64 (release arm included) and cross-checks `_fmode` against `_get_fmode` and `_environ` against `getenv`; extern_data_import_pe is its extern-DATA sibling and explains why NEITHER of these names can play that role.
